title: The Fox and the Monkey

full_text:
Upon the death of the Lion King, the animals of the forest assembled to elect a new sovereign. A nimble monkey leaped into the clearing, danced upon his hands, turned acrobatic somersaults, and made such comical, charming grimaces that the delighted beasts broke into wild applause and immediately proclaimed the Monkey their new King!

The fox alone was deeply displeased that an agile clown had been chosen to govern the realm.

A few days later, the fox discovered a hunter's iron spring-trap set in a thicket, baited with a plump piece of roasted meat. The fox hurried to the royal court, bowed low before the Monkey King, and whispered with great reverence:

"Sire, while walking in the forest, I discovered a hidden treasure of rich meat. By ancient law, all treasure belongs to the King; I have left it untouched so that your majesty may claim it with his own royal hands!"

Flattered by the fox's submission, the greedy monkey rushed to the spot and grasped the meat. The iron jaws of the trap snapped shut with a violent CLANG, pinning the monkey's arm fast against the wood!

The monkey shrieked in agony, struggling helplessly while the fox looked on with cool composure. "You treacherous knave!" cried the trapped monarch. "You led your King into a deadly snare!"

The fox smiled and answered: "A King? With such an empty head and such childish greed, did you truly imagine you had the wisdom to govern a kingdom?"
moral: A crown without wisdom brings swift disaster upon both ruler and kingdom.
